title: Fallback Cascades: Never Dead
objective: After this lesson you will be able to design tiered fallback cascades (retry → smaller model → cached → deterministic → human) with per-tier triggers and honesty labels, and chaos-test the primary-down path quarterly.
why: Models outage, rate limits bite, latency spikes at peak — and 'error page for all' forfeits trust built over months. Cascades degrade gracefully: each tier weaker but working, each labeled honestly (stale/cached/simplified), ending at humans with full context, never at dead ends. Reliability is tiered degradation designed upfront, not heroics during outages.

blocks.text: Five tiers, each with a **trigger** (when to drop) and a **label** (what users see): (1) primary model; (2) retry + secondary/smaller model on timeout/error; (3) cached/stale-labeled answers; (4) deterministic safe mode (status + human queue, no generation); (5) human takeover with attached context. Labels preserve trust ('cached answer from 2h ago' beats silent staleness); triggers automate descent (no human deciding mid-outage).

blocks.caption: Descend on failure, label every tier, terminate at humans

blocks.text: Below all models sits **deterministic safe mode**: order status from DB reads, templated acknowledgments, human-queue routing — zero model calls, always available. Safe mode handles 30–60% of traffic acceptably (status checks, FAQs) while models recover. Systems without a model-free floor have no floor: total outages instead of degraded service.

Untested fallbacks are wishes: quarterly **chaos drills** disable the primary path and verify each tier engages (secondary answers, cache labels appear, safe mode holds, humans receive context). Measure descent time and tier accuracy during drills; fix gaps in peacetime. The drill that embarrasses in staging prevents the outage that pages at peak.

blocks.title: Descend the cascade
blocks.note: Static trace version (async runners need top-level await): tiers primary→secondary→cached, terminal human-queue. The lesson code shows the live pattern; this trace proves the ordering and terminal. Full async behavior is covered by the verify harness note below.

items: Five tiers (primary → secondary → cached-labeled → deterministic → human) with triggers + honesty labels
Deterministic safe mode is the floor: zero-model service for status/FAQs/queueing
Chaos-test primary-down quarterly: descent, labels, and human context verified in peacetime

exercise.prompt: (a) Trace the practice cascade tiers and terminal. (b) Write the label each tier shows users (fresh/stale-labeled/safe-mode/human-queue with context). (c) Design the chaos drill: what gets disabled, what gets measured, what constitutes pass/fail.
hints: Tiers descend primary→secondary→cached; human-queue terminates. Labels travel with tiers.
Labels: fresh (tier 1-2), 'cached 2h ago' (tier 3), 'limited mode' (safe), 'agent joining with full context' (queue).
Drill: disable primary; measure descent time + tier accuracy + label presence; pass = degraded service with honest labels inside SLA.
exercise.why: Tier tracing (ordering), label design (honesty), and drill design (verification) are the three reliability judgments — each concrete, each scheduled, none heroic.
exercise.code: // Cascade pattern: triggers descend, labels honestly, humans terminate.

quiz.q: Primary model down at peak. Correct system behavior?
options: Tiered descent (secondary → cached-labeled → deterministic → human queue): degraded with honest labels, never dead
quiz.explain: Reliability tiers trade capability for availability stepwise, labeled honestly. Dead is the only unacceptable tier.

quiz.q: Cached fallback answers without labels. Problem?
options: Silent staleness destroys trust: cached tiers must label age ('2h ago') so users calibrate
quiz.explain: Honesty labels preserve trust during degradation. Unlabeled stale answers are lies that surface later, worse.

options: Wishes: untested descent paths fail at peak — quarterly drills verify tiers, labels, and human context
quiz.explain: Descent verified in peacetime or discovered in incidents. Drills measure what outages would: time, accuracy, labels.

summary: Tiered descent with triggers, honesty labels per tier, deterministic floor, quarterly chaos proof. Degraded beats dead, labeled beats silent.
